title: Anthony Joshua Returns to the Ring in Jeddah With India’s Nishant Dev on Undercard
excerpt: Two-time heavyweight champion faces Kristian Prenga on Saturday in his emotional comeback after a tragic car crash, with a Tyson Fury mega-fight potentially on the line.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Anthony Joshua faces Kristian Prenga in his first fight since a tragic car crash.
  • A victory for Joshua could lead to a mega-fight against Tyson Fury.
  • Nishant Dev, an Indian boxer, competes on the undercard against Cesar Diaz.
  • Joshua is a -4500 favorite against Prenga, who has a perfect knockout record.

Joshua's Betting Odds
  • Anthony Joshua is set to fight Albanian heavyweight Kristian Prenga in Jeddah, marking his return to the ring after a December knockout victory and a tragic car accident in Nigeria.
  • Joshua, a two-time unified heavyweight champion, views the fight as a crucial checkpoint in his career and enters as a heavy betting favorite.
  • Prenga, with a perfect knockout ratio, faces a significant challenge as this 12-round bout is his first against a top-tier opponent.
  • The fight is part of a strategic plan that could lead to a highly anticipated matchup between Joshua and Tyson Fury if both emerge victorious.

Anthony Joshua steps back into the ring on Saturday at the Jeddah Superdome in Saudi Arabia, facing Albanian heavyweight Kristian Prenga in a bout that serves as both an emotional comeback and a gateway to boxing’s most anticipated superfight.

It will be Joshua’s first fight since a December knockout of Jake Paul in Miami — and his first since a car accident in Nigeria just 10 days after that victory killed two of his closest friends, Sina Ghami and Latif Adoyele.

Beyond the Boxing

Joshua, 36, has spoken openly about the emotional weight of returning to competition. He has been training alongside former undisputed heavyweight champion Oleksandr Usyk in Valencia, Spain, since January — a camp he said forced him to “drop his ego” from the start.

“The reality of the matter is there is no universe, there is no future unless I get past this checkpoint on Saturday night.”

— Anthony Joshua

The two-time unified heavyweight champion (29-4, 26 KOs) enters as a -4500 betting favorite. But Joshua has insisted he is taking nothing for granted, describing the fight as a checkpoint rather than a formality.

Prenga: Albania’s Power Puncher

Prenga (20-1, 20 KOs) brings a perfect knockout ratio in his 20 victories but a largely untested resume. The 35-year-old New Jersey-based Albanian has never been scheduled for more than a 10-round fight. His most recent bout was a first-round stoppage of journeyman Joe Jones (16-15-2) in Atlantic City in February.

Saturday’s 12-round heavyweight contest represents an enormous step up in class. Prenga has dismissed the notion that he is merely a warm-up act. “This is everything for me. It’s not just for me, this is for all my country. This is the biggest event for Albania,” he said at the pre-fight press conference.

The Fury Endgame

The fight card is the first half of a calculated two-fight sequence. If Joshua beats Prenga on Saturday and Tyson Fury defeats Mariusz Wach in Thailand on Friday, the stage would be set for what promoters are billing as the biggest fight in British boxing history.

A Joshua-Fury bout has been years in the making, frustrated by contractual disputes, pandemic-era delays, and both fighters’ losses to Oleksandr Usyk. Saturday’s result will determine whether the superfight finally moves from speculation to the schedule.

Undercard Highlights
›Nishant Dev: 9-2-0 record, former youth world champion.
›Cesar Diaz: 10-2 record, facing Dev on the undercard.
›Hamzah Sheeraz defends super-middleweight title.
›Josh Kelly defends super-welterweight belt.

Nishant Dev Flies the Indian Flag

Indian boxing fans have reason to tune into the Jeddah card beyond the heavyweight main event. Nishant Dev, the Indian super-welterweight with a professional record of 9-2-0, faces 10-2 Cesar Diaz on the undercard.

Dev, a former youth amateur world champion who turned professional in 2024, has been steadily building his career on the international circuit. His inclusion on a card headlined by Joshua in Saudi Arabia marks a significant platform boost for Indian professional boxing, which has historically struggled for mainstream visibility.

Stacked Undercard

The supporting bouts include Hamzah Sheeraz defending his super-middleweight world title against Simon Zachenhuber, Josh Kelly defending his super-welterweight belt against Caoimhin Agyarko, and 2024 Olympic gold medalist Oleksandr Khyzhniak making his second professional appearance.

The card begins at 6 PM local time in Jeddah (8:30 AM ET / 6 PM IST) on Saturday, July 25, with the main event expected around 11 PM local. The bout will be broadcast on DAZN.
